few ppl know the sierras like i do. I have backpacked, hiked, camped, toured into sierras over 50 yrs, both east and westside. Sequoia NP was 
my playground. The eastern wall is always a splendid sight after you travel along 395 from LA for 4 hrs and are just entering lone pine. I did most 
lateral trails from the east wall trailheads off 395 to the sierra ridge. I did both mt whitney and forester pass in 1992, My backpacking was mostly in 90s but  after i switched to car camping due to age i always 
did mammoth area for day hikes  and stayed ar glass creek free USDA site which was my base camp.

My first expedition into the Sierra was the HST from Cresent Meadow in Sequoia to 395 and a 2 day hitch-hike back to my motorcycle.
1972 .  Rambled most of the area from Yosemite south since then. Spent a few seasons packing mules for Reds. Kept pretty busy, lived it, and the office views are always stunning.  Retired now and have a small ranch overlooking the San Joaquin River, 900ft below.

comments.author: @JonChristenson-b3v4m
comments.text:
When I was younger I took a back packing trip to an area called CHAIN OF LAKES and camped there for about 6 days of the most unforgettable adventure of my life in the Sierra Nevada Mountains that changed my world view of how important  nature can heal the anxiety of the digital world. I became aware of a change within my own body. I started for first time in my life  to relax and enjoy my life /free from the expectations of mankind. One day I took a swim in one of the lakes and I was transformed as I swam around the submerged trees in the lake.
 I felt like a fish and this experience has lived within my imagination to this day and now I am 83 years and I am thankful that our nation has preserved these holy places of peace and quiet.
